en: Fold line annotations for UCLA Alphonso & Imogene trade card

body.value: Hinge of the lower flap at approximately 62.6% of the expanded image height. Located by the notch the crease cuts in the card's right edge in the expanded photograph, and confirmed by the collapsed card's lower edge coinciding with the same row. Everything below this line is the flap.

Approximately 25.2% of the expanded image height. This is where the flap's free edge lands when it is folded up through 180 degrees, derived as the crease position minus the flap length (37.4%). It is not a fold in the paper.

One continuous front sheet with a single hinged flap below the crease; the upper sheet never moves. Swinging the flap upward through 180 degrees turns its verso to the viewer and covers the lower part of the sheet, including the sitters' bodies, so that only their faces remain visible. The verso is not visible in the fully expanded photograph, because in that state it is face-down; it is recovered as a region of the collapsed photograph. Flipping the card reveals the back, for which only a collapsed photograph exists, so the demo folds the flap flat before flipping.
